source_refs.note: Exercise 4.3, Question 10: book page 77 (PDF 82); answer key PDF 303

blocks.prompt: 10 Use the matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\) to encode the message: KEEP IT UP, where letters \(A\) to \(Z\) are corresponding to the numbers 1 to 26.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh encoding (cryptography) ka sawal hai, Example 17 jaisa, bas matrix \(3 \times 3\) hai.
Coded columns nikalne hain.
Plan: letters se numbers, teen teen ke groups (aakhri group poora karna), har column ko \(A\) se zarb, aur decode kar ke tasdeeq.
Dhyan dein: group banate waqt words ke beech ki space ko letter nahi ginte. Aakhri group adhoora ho to khaali jagah par koi tay shuda number (yahan 0) rakhte hain, aur message bhejne wale aur parhne wale dono ko yeh shart maloom honi chahiye. Zarb hamesha \(A \times \text{column}\) hota hai, \(\text{column} \times A\) nahi.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\), message KEEP IT UP, aur A se Z tak letters = 1 se 26.
Humein find karna hai: coded (khufia) message.
Tareeqa: Example 17 ki tarah letters ko numbers mein badlenge, teen teen ke groups banayenge (kyunke \(A\) \(3 \times 3\) hai), har group ko \(3 \times 1\) column likh kar left side se \(A\) se zarb denge.

Letters ko numbers mein badlein aur teen teen ke groups banayein
K = 11, E = 5, E = 5, P = 16, I = 9, T = 20, U = 21, P = 16.
Groups: KEE, PIT, UP. Aakhri group mein sirf do letters hain, is liye teesri jagah 0 rakha.
\[\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 9 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 16 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(3 \times 3\) matrix sirf \(3 \times 1\) column se zarb ho sakta hai, is liye har group mein teen numbers chahiye. Words ke beech ki space code nahi ki. 0 ka matlab hai koi letter nahi (khaali jagah); answer key bhi yahi karti hai.

KEE ko code karein
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(11) + 0(5) + 1(5) = 16\]
\[2(11) + (-1)(5) + 1(5) = 22\]
\[0(11) + 1(5) + 2(5) = 15\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 22 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har entry \(A\) ki ek row aur column ka zarb hai: pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama.

PIT ko code karein
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 9 \\ 20\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(16) + 0(9) + 1(20) = 36\]
\[2(16) + (-1)(9) + 1(20) = 43\]
\[0(16) + 1(9) + 2(20) = 49\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}36 \\ 43 \\ 49\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har entry \(A\) ki ek row aur column ka zarb hai: pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama.

UP ko code karein
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 16 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\]
\[1(21) + 0(16) + 1(0) = 21\]
\[2(21) + (-1)(16) + 1(0) = 26\]
\[0(21) + 1(16) + 2(0) = 16\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 26 \\ 16\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har entry \(A\) ki ek row aur column ka zarb hai: pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama.

Tasdeeq: ek group ko wapas decode karein
\(|A| = -1\) hai, to \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\):
\[A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 22 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -5 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Decode karne par wapas KEE ke numbers 11, 5, 5 milne chahiye, aur mil gaye. Is se pata chalta hai ke encoding sahi hai aur receiver message parh sakta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: KEEP IT UP mein 8 letters hain, is liye teen teen ke groups mein aakhri group (UP) mein ek jagah khaali reh jati hai. Sawal yeh nahi batata ke us jagah kya rakhein; answer key ka aakhri column \([21, 26, 16]\) khaali jagah par 0 rakhne se aata hai. Is shart ke saath key ka jawab \([16, 22, 15]\), \([36, 43, 49]\), \([21, 26, 16]\) sahi hai.
